map.rationale: The ground storey reads as a SMOOTH, neatly coursed grey ashlar plane — regular rectangular blocks with tight joints — the dressed-stone wall body, distinct from the rough corner stone.

map.role: corner quoins, plinth course & chimney shaft (rough grey stone)
map.rationale: The building corners and the chimney shaft show a LUMPY, irregular speckled grey grain — same cool tone as the wall but a coarser cobble texture; kept separate from stone_bricks so the quoin/buttress distinction survives a mean-color match.

map.role: half-timbering frame — vertical studs, corner posts, eaves beams
map.rationale: The signature dark vertical stripes over the cream panels are heavy round structural timbers with a strong wood grain — the framing rhythm; the dark-brown LOG texture (not flat planks) is what reads here.

map.role: upper-storey plaster infill between the timbers
map.rationale: The panels between the studs are a warm, matte CREAM off-white — not pure white and not the cool grey stone below; white_terracotta gives the soft plaster tone without collapsing into the stone base.

The steep roof slopes are stepped courses of warm MEDIUM-brown sawn planks — clearly lighter and flatter-grained than the near-black dark_oak timber frame; spruce_planks holds that distinct, lighter roof tone.

map.role: roof eaves, verge & rake fascia (darker plank edge)
map.rationale: The overhanging eaves and gable rake read noticeably DARKER than the roof field — a deeper plank banding the roof edge; a near-tone pair with spruce_planks kept distinct (dark edge over lighter field).
The chimney top is a warm RED-BROWN coursed brick block crowning the cool grey cobble shaft — a deliberate warm-on-cool material contrast, not the same stone as the shaft.

entry.rationale: The ground-floor doorway shows a warm-brown panelled wooden door set in the stone reveal — a spruce-toned timber door.
Both storeys show brown LATTICE/slatted window fills and flanking shutters with a fine horizontal grain — trapdoor slats read this gridded reveal far better than a solid plank.
A single glowing warm light hangs beside the front door in the concept — a lantern accent at the entrance.
